title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_1RE0LD_0RE0LF_0LB0RA_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_1RE0LD_0RE0LF_0LB0RA_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It has a twin, which differs only in what A does on a 1. This page lists what is established, sorted by what each result rests on; the counter at its left end is understood, the work zone that drives it is not.
verdict: The question is open. It halts only when F reads a 1, which has not happened in 5·1011 steps. The tape holds three counters: a binary counter at the left end, a second binary counter in the middle whose overflow increments it, and a tail of irregular gaps at the right that the middle counter reads at every count. Lean proves the increment of the left counter and the reset, carry and settle rules of the middle one; the tail has no known rule, and a halt could only come from there.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Three shift rules for all n and any surrounding tape: E crosses (110)^n leaving (010)^n, D crosses (011)^n leaving (001)^n, and B crosses (100)^n leaving (101)^n.

claims.title: The increment of the left counter
claims.text: For every n and any tape around it, L 1000 (1010)^n C>1 1 R reaches L 1010 1 (0001)^n 0 D> R in 12n+8 steps: C walks left over n one-digits 1010, turns the zero-digit 1000 into a one, and B walks back turning each one-digit into a zero-digit. A1 is not used, so the same theorem holds for both twins.

claims.title: The middle counter
claims.text: Right of the 11 that ends the left counter sits a second binary counter of 4-cell digits, 0001 (zero) and 0101 (one). Four rules, for every number of digits and any tape around them: a cycle starts with L B> (1010)^n R → L (0001)^n B> R (n zero digits, 4n steps); a carry L 0001 (0101)^c 0001 F> 0000 R → L 0101 (0001)^c 0 0 F> 0001 0 1 R (12c + 42 steps) turns the c trailing ones into zeros and the zero above them into a one; and a settle step L 0001 (0101)^c 0 0 F> 0001 y z R → L 0101 (0001)^c 0001 F> 0 0 y z R (12c + 32 steps, for y z = 01 and 00) counts once more. A1 is not used, so the theorems hold for both twins.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 182 cells have been visited and 71 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
No halt in the first 5·10<sup>11</sup> steps
Where the twins differ
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps A reads a 1 only 11 times, always with 0s on both sides; F reads only 0s, followed by a 0.

claims.title: A binary counter at the left end
claims.text: Whenever the head is at least 8 cells right of the counter, the tape from the left end reads 1010101101010110, then 4-cell digits 1010 (one) and 1000 (zero), then 11. Read as a binary number (least significant digit on the right) this counter goes up at almost every change. From step 6.3·106 to 109 the decoded value changes 529,577 times; 529,571 changes are increases, 4 are overflows where the counter gains a digit (18 → 21 digits), and 2 are not classified. At 109 steps it has 20 digits.

claims.title: Three counters, one inside the next
claims.text: Between two increments of the left counter the head runs the middle counter from its reset up to its overflow; each count ends with F at the right end of the middle counter, where the next cells of tape (the tail) are read and rewritten (the carry and settle rules above move a 0 1 into and out of the tail). The overflow of the middle counter is swept back to (1010)^n and passed left as one increment of the left counter. For 2a the number of steps per left increment is constant over long stretches: in each of the windows of 2.5·108 steps from 5·108 to 1.5·109 there are exactly 53,010 ± 1 increments (4,716.1 steps and 124.5 F visits each). It changes only near overflows of the left counter: per 109 steps, 1,888 steps per increment in the first 109 steps, then 4,500, 4,094, 4,495, 8,612 (5·109 to 8·109), 3,698, 2,844, 4,374, and 5,918 from 1.3·1010 to 1.7·1010. The left counter grows from 18 to 23 digits in that time.

claims.title: A reads a 1 only at overflows
claims.text: A reads a 1 only when the left counter overflows (gains a digit). After the first 2.8·10<sup>6</sup> steps, A1 is read 16 times in 1.75·10<sup>10</sup> steps, in 8 bursts at steps 1.8·10<sup>7</sup>, 1.9·10<sup>8</sup>, 4.5·10<sup>8</sup>, 1.7·10<sup>9</sup>, 3.8·10<sup>9</sup>, 8.3·10<sup>9</sup>, 1.1·10<sup>10</sup> and 1.75·10<sup>10</sup>, each within 5,000 steps of an overflow found by the counter decoder (18 → 23 digits). So the twins can only part at overflows of the left counter.

claims.title: Not decided by n-gram CPS up to width 14
claims.text: The n-gram Closed Position Set decider (tools/c/ngramcps.c) with equal widths 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14, plain and with the fixed-length (1) and LRU history augmentations, either reaches a halting local configuration (UNKNOWN) or stops at 3·107 local configurations: it does not prove non-halting at these settings.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/fixed
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: Late in the run the tape is made of long stretches of (0 1)^n, (0^3 1)^n and (1^2 0)^n; both ends grow, the right one by single cells at irregular times (e.g. 2a: cell 175 at step 4.7·108). The stretches (0 1)^n and (0^3 1)^n are the digits 1010 and 1000 of the left binary counter read with another phase (see below).

claims.title: The (110)^n block at the right end
claims.text: At the right end a block (110)^n grows by one word at some of the right records (for 2a, n = 12, 13, 14 at the right records at 4.7·108, 5.8·108 and 9.6·108 steps). It is the far end of the tail (see above).

claims.title: The tail is an irregular list of gaps
claims.text: Right of the middle counter the tape is a list of gaps between single 1s. Read at the start of each cycle (2a, near step 3·108), its first few gaps run through three phases, one per cycle, and the rest of the list changes once every three cycles, in a way that looks like a rewriting system on gap lengths (for example 14 → 0 1 0 1 8 → 0 1 2 8 → 2 3 1 5 → 0 4 0 1 5 → 3 4 5 → 8 5 → ...). The configuration of tail and middle counter at an increment of the left counter never repeated in the first 3·109 steps (996,093 increments, compared by hash; holdouts/1RB1RD_1LC0RD_1RE0LD_0RE0LF_0LB0RA_0LC---/c/zper.c). The right end of the tape grows a few cells (3 to 8) at a time, at irregular steps. No rule for the tail has been found.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when F reads a 1. The left counter and the middle counter are understood and their moves are proved; what is missing is a rule for the tail, which the middle counter reads at every count and which decides when the right end grows. A halt would have to come from the tail.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two machines that part at step 132
html: This machine and its twin, 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_... (2a) and 1RB1RF_1LC0RD_... (2b), differ only in what state A does when it reads a 1: 2a goes to D, 2b to F. A reads a 1 very rarely, and only when the counter at the left end of the tape gains a digit. The first such read is at step 132, and after it the two runs differ, but they are built the same way.

sections.heading: Three counters, one inside the next
html: The left end of the tape is a binary counter. After a short fixed prefix it is a row of 4-cell digits: 1010 means 1 and 1000 means 0, least significant on the right, ended by 11. To add one, the head arrives in state C on that 11, runs left over the trailing ones, changes the first zero into a one, and runs back in state B changing the ones it passed into zeros. Lean proves this move for any number of trailing ones.

Right of the 11 is a second binary counter, with digits 0001 (zero) and 0101 (one). A cycle starts with the head in state B in front of (1010)^n, which it rewrites into n zero digits. Then it counts: each count ends with F at the right end of the middle counter, and a carry or settle move adds one (Lean proves both for any number of carried digits). When the middle counter overflows, it is swept back to (1010)^n and the head carries one increment into the left counter. So the left counter counts the cycles of the middle one.

Right of the middle counter is the tail: a list of gaps between single 1s. Each count of the middle counter reads and rewrites the first cells of the tail, so the tail changes a little at every cycle: its first gaps run through three phases, one per cycle, and the rest changes once every three cycles. The right end of the tape grows by a few cells at long, irregular intervals. The stretches (0 1)^n and (0^3 1)^n seen on the tape are digits of the two counters, read with another phase.

sections.heading: What the tail does is unknown
html: The two counters are understood and their moves are proved. The tail is not: it decides how many steps a cycle takes (constant over long stretches, then changing near overflows of the left counter) and when the right end grows, and a halt (F reading a 1) could only come from the way the middle counter meets it. A proof either way needs a rule for the tail, and none has been found; its gap lists look like a small rewriting system rather than a counter.

The twins differ only when A reads a 1, and that happens only when the left counter overflows, a few times per 1010 steps. At such a read in 2b (step 2.26·109) the fixed prefix of its counter changed to the one 2a has; the two runs are built the same way but are not the same run.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).
After 109 steps the tape spans 182 cells (42 left of the start, 133 right), with a density of 1s of 0.39.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Binary counter fed by a work zone (1RB1R?_1LC0RD_1RE0LD_0RE0LF_0LB0RA_0LC--- twins)
summary: Twin 2a: three counters, one inside the next: a proved binary counter at the left end, a middle binary counter whose carry rules are proved in Lean, and an irregular gap list (the tail) that the middle counter reads at every count; open.
